speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. As your doctor, I need to understand your condition; since you are a newborn, I will ask your caregiver these questions. How long has your baby been having symptoms, and what specific signs have you noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the lack of prenatal care and immunization history, is your newborn exhibiting signs of respiratory distress, such as grunting, nasal flaring, or retractions? REQUEST TEST: CBC, Blood_Culture, G6PD_Assay.

speaker: Doctor
text: The test results are normal, which is good news. However, since your newborn has no immunization history and lacked prenatal care, do you notice any yellowing of the skin or eyes, or any unusual discoloration? Also, has the baby had any fever or feeding difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (likely a PDA), bluish non-blanching macules (petechiae), cloudy lenses (cataracts), and hearing loss represents the classic triad of congenital rubella. Given the lack of prenatal care, the mother was likely infected during pregnancy.
